result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.transform_to_subgraph_ws()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Create a subgraph from current selection. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L16557-L16689){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.transform_to_subgraph_ws() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Subgraph from the selection](/assets/graphs/transform-to-subgraph-ws.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Left: nodes A, B, C, and E are selected in the accent color. Right: the new graph keeps just those four nodes and the three edges among them, A–B, B–C, and B–E; nodes D and F and every edge touching them are dropped, shown dashed." width="100%"} Extracts the currently selected nodes and/or edges into a new Graph object. The behavior depends on what's selected: - nodes selected: include those nodes plus all edges between them - edges selected: include those edges plus their endpoint nodes - both selected: uses node selection (ignores edge selection) All node and edge attributes are preserved in the subgraph. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : New Graph object containing the subgraph. Has same directedness as original graph. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Extract a node-induced subgraph: ::: {#1a82db90 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph(directed=True).add_path_graph(n=6) # Get node IDs for nodes at positions 2, 3, 4 all_node_ids = list(graph.get_node_ids(limit=None)) node_ids_to_select = [all_node_ids[2], all_node_ids[3], all_node_ids[4]] graph.select_nodes_by_id(node_ids=node_ids_to_select) subgraph = graph.transform_to_subgraph_ws() # Returns 3 subgraph.count_nodes() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 3 ``` ::: ::: ::: {#dae483ce .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Returns 2 (edges between selected nodes) subgraph.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 2 ``` ::: ::: Extract an edge-induced subgraph instead by selecting edges rather than nodes: ::: {#d98d5fec .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph().add_cycle_graph(5) edges = graph.get_edge_ids()[:2] graph.select_edges_by_id(edges) subgraph = graph.transform_to_subgraph_ws() subgraph.count_nodes(), subgraph.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` (3, 2) ``` ::: :::
